General Dental Services in Phoenix, AZ --> Home About Us Services Services Overview General Dentistry Cosmetic Dentistry Restorative Dentistry Special Dentistry Our Difference Patients Patient Education Contact Contact Menu (602) 997-6440 (602) 956-1310 GENERAL DENTISTRY PHOENIX AZ Regular check-ups, cleanings and oral examinations Oral Hygiene Oral hygiene is the practice of keeping the mouth and teeth clean to prevent tooth decay and gum disease. This includes a daily routine of brushing teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, flossing, using an antiseptic mouthwash, as well as avoiding sugary and acidic foods.  Regular dental check-ups and cleanings, along with maintaining a healthy diet and lifestyle, can help to ensure that the teeth and gums stay healthy and strong. Cleaning by a dental hygienist is a routine procedure that involves removing plaque and tartar from the teeth. This is done through scaling and polishing, as well as flossing and fluoride treatment. A cleaning can help to prevent tooth decay and gum disease, and is usually recommended to be done every six months.  A dental hygienist will also provide oral hygiene instructions and education. REQUEST APPOINTMENT Periodontal Services Periodontal services refer to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the gums, the bones that support the teeth, and the surrounding soft tissue.  These services include scaling and root planing, which is a deep cleaning procedure that removes plaque and tartar from the teeth, as well as laser therapy to remove bacteria and infected tissue.  Periodontal treatment is important in preventing and managing gum disease and preserving the health of the gums, teeth, and bones. It's essential for patients to maintain regular periodontal check-ups and cleanings, which is usually recommended to be done every three to four months. REQUEST APPOINTMENT Examination A clinical dental examination is a comprehensive evaluation of a patient's oral health, performed by a dentist. The examination includes an assessment of the teeth, gums, tongue, and surrounding tissue, including the lips, cheeks, and floor and roof of the mouth.  The dentist will also check for any signs of oral cancer, decay, or other issues, such as tooth wear, bite problems and jaw  disorders. Additionally, imaging will detect any underlying issues that may not be visible during a visual examination.  Digital Imaging The dentist will then provide a diagnosis and treatment plan. It's recommended for patients to undergo a clinical dental examination at least twice a year. REQUEST APPOINTMENT Dental Screenings: Oral Cancer rates have been on the rise in the past decade. Special Services in Phoenix, AZ --> Home About Us Services Services Overview General Dentistry Cosmetic Dentistry Restorative Dentistry Special Dentistry Our Difference Patients Patient Education Contact Contact Menu (602) 997-6440 (602) 956-1310 SPECIAL DENTISTRY PHOENIX AZ We Put You First At Every Visit TMJ Mouthguards TMJ (Temporomandibular joint) disorder is a condition that affects the jaw joint and the surrounding muscles, resulting in pain and discomfort in the jaw, face, neck, and shoulders.  Common symptoms include jaw pain, headaches, clicking or popping sounds in the jaw joint, and difficulty opening or closing the mouth.  The causes of TMJ can be varied and can include injury, stress, or misalignment of the jaw.  Treatment options may include physical therapy, medication, or in some cases, surgery.  Dentists and oral surgeons are typically the first point of contact for diagnosis and treatment of TMJ disorders. REQUEST APPOINTMENT Sports Mouthguards Sports Mouthguards are essential for athletes who participate in contact sports to protect their teeth, gums and tongue from injury. They are made from a soft, flexible material that mold to the shape of the wearer's teeth and provide a cushion against impacts. It is recommended to get a custom-fit mouthguard from a dental professional for maximum protection and comfort during games and practices.
